question:
The following text is adapted from John Matheus's 1926 short story "Mr. Bradford Teaches Sunday School." In this scene, Mr. Bradford is driving through the Florida countryside.

Up in the tall water oaks, the moss had come alive with a green, silvery sheen, draping down like carnival streamers or like the somber trimmings hung to mourn the dead. The pines glowed a brilliant green. Bald cypresses stretched out along the waterways, and the willows drooped and wept as they forever do. Mr. Bradford took in this magnificent display of nature all around him.

As used in the text, what does the word "display" most nearly mean?
subject: Reading and Writing
tags: vocabulary in context, words in context
shortexplanation: In context, the "display" of nature refers to the grand showing of the scenery, so "exhibition" fits best.
longexplanation: The passage lavishly describes the moss, pines, cypresses, and willows as a splendid showing of natural beauty that Mr. Bradford takes in. Here "display" names this magnificent presentation, which matches "exhibition." "Concealment" is the opposite of showing something, while "similarity" and "pretentiousness" do not fit the celebratory description of the landscape.

question:
Sarah Marquis trekked 16,000 kilometers across Asia, Siberia, and Australia—an unquestionably impressive feat—but when it comes to ______ a lasting place in history for oneself, few things work better than being the first to accomplish something. Consider that people will always recall that Anesia Pinheiro Machado was the first woman in Brazil to carry passengers as a pilot and the first to perform stunt flights.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The blank needs a word meaning to create or secure a lasting legacy, so "establish" fits.
longexplanation: The sentence argues that being first is the most effective way to secure a lasting historical legacy, a point illustrated by Machado's firsts in aviation. "Establish" means to bring about or set up such a legacy and fits the logic precisely. "Recognize" means merely to identify, while "undermine" and "constrain" carry negative meanings that contradict the idea of building a legacy.

question:
Text 1
Analyzing the overall chemistry of rock-core samples drilled from Australia's Mount McRae Shale, Ariel Anbar and colleagues detected a brief but notable spike in molybdenum (Mo) at a depth corresponding to about 2.5 billion years ago (Ga). Because Mo on Earth is liberated chiefly by the oxidative weathering of minerals, Anbar's team concluded that atmospheric oxygen rose momentarily 2.5 Ga before falling back to its previously negligible level.

Text 2
Sarah Slotznick and colleagues took a second look at the same Mount McRae Shale core. Aware that bulk chemical analysis can hide contextual clues, they added high-resolution microscopy, which exposed volcanic debris—a known carrier of Mo—dating to roughly 2.5 Ga, along with tiny fractures running through the surrounding rock. According to the team, fluids could have seeped through those microfractures to reach the debris and triggered oxidative weathering long after the debris was first deposited.

Based on the texts, Anbar et al. (Text 1) and Slotznick et al. (Text 2) would most likely disagree over the answer to which question about the section of the Mount McRae Shale rock-core corresponding to 2.5 Ga?
option a: Is the increase in Mo in that portion attributable to oxidative weathering of the material found in that portion?
option b: Is the increase in Mo in that portion indicative of an increase in atmospheric oxygen dating to the same time?
option c: Did chemically analyzing bulk samples lead to a false impression that there is an increase in Mo in that portion?
option d: Does the increase in Mo in that portion suggest that atmospheric oxygen levels were not negligible before 2.5Ga?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Both teams agree Mo increased, but they disagree about whether that increase reflects a real rise in atmospheric oxygen at 2.5 Ga.
longexplanation: Anbar's team reads the Mo spike as evidence that atmospheric oxygen briefly increased 2.5 Ga. Slotznick's team argues the Mo could have arrived much later through fluids moving in microfractures, so it need not signal higher oxygen at that time. The two groups would therefore disagree about whether the Mo increase indicates a rise in atmospheric oxygen dating to the same period. The other options describe points on which the texts either agree or say nothing.

question:
The Federalist Papers consist of 85 essays composed by Alexander Hamilton, John Jay, and James Madison. Published under a pseudonym in the New York Packet and other New York newspapers during 1787–88, they urged New Yorkers to vote to ratify the proposed United States Constitution. The authorship of most individual essays is settled, but a handful remain in question: No. 6, "Concerning Dangers from Dissensions between the States," was certainly Hamilton's work, whereas No. 62, "The Senate," might have been written by either Hamilton or Madison.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
option a: The text lists the authors of a collection of essays and then notes that some of the essays were written by one person, while others were written by two people.
option b: The text describes why a collection of essays is notable and then details its publication history.
option c: The text summarizes an argument made in a collection of essays and then suggests that the essays' authors didn't unanimously agree with the argument.
option d: The text mentions a collection of essays and then points out something about these essays that is not completely known.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The text introduces the essays and then notes that the authorship of a few remains uncertain—something not completely known.
longexplanation: The passage first presents the Federalist Papers and their purpose, then observes that although most essays' authorship is settled, a few (such as No. 62) are disputed. This amounts to pointing out something about the essays that is not completely known. Choice A misstates the authorship split, and choices B and C emphasize publication history or disagreement with the argument that the text does not actually develop.

question:
"Aunt Sue's Stories" is a 1926 poem by Langston Hughes. In the poem, the speaker makes clear that the tales Aunt Sue shares are drawn from her own lived experience, stating that ______

Which choice most effectively uses a quotation from "Aunt Sue's Stories" to illustrate the claim?
option a: a listening child "knows that Aunt Sue / Never got her stores out of any book at all, / But that they came / Right out of her own life."
option b: the people in the stories "Mingle themselves softly / In the flow of old Aunt Sue's voice, / Mingle themselves softly."
option c: dark shadows "cross and recross / Aunt Sues stories."
option d: the stories are told during "Summer nights on the front porch."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice A quotes lines saying the stories came "Right out of her own life," directly illustrating that they are based on Aunt Sue's own experiences.
longexplanation: The claim is that Aunt Sue's stories draw on her personal experiences. Choice A quotes the child's understanding that Aunt Sue never took the stories "out of any book at all" but that "they came / Right out of her own life," which directly supports the claim. The other quotations describe the storytelling's mood, imagery, or setting rather than the personal source of the stories.

question:
Auxins are plant hormones that shape growth, among them leaf orientation—the tendency for one side of a leaf, along its long central axis, to be larger than the other. Ciera Martinez, a biologist at the University of California, Berkeley, and her colleagues observed that in some plants whose leaves grow in pairs, auxins usually gather on opposite sides of the two leaves (for instance, the left side of one leaf and the right side of its partner). From this they predicted that paired leaves would tend to show opposite-side orientation, and they tested the idea by studying paired leaves from several grapevine species.

Orientation of Leaf Pairs in Grapevines (Number of pairs vs. Orientation of leaves in pair, for Amur grape, July grape, and graybark grape):

| Orientation | Amur grape | July grape | graybark grape |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| opposite side | ~148 | ~202 | ~267 |
| same side | ~60 | ~102 | ~92 |

Which choice best describes data from the graph that support Martinez and colleagues’ hypothesis?
option a: Although the number of leaf pairs showing same-side orientation is fairly high in the July grape, it is much lower in both the Amur grape and graybark grape.
option b: In the graybark grape, Amur grape, and July grape, all the leaf pairs show opposite-side orientation.
option c: Although the exact ratio varies by species, the graybark grape, Amur grape, and July grape all show more leaf pairs with opposite-side orientations than with same-side orientations.
option d: The number of leaf pairs showing opposite-side orientation is fairly high in the July grape, but not as high as it is in the graybark grape.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: In all three species, opposite-side pairs outnumber same-side pairs, which supports the hypothesis.
longexplanation: Martinez's team predicted that paired leaves would tend toward opposite-side orientation. The table shows opposite-side pairs exceeding same-side pairs in every species: roughly 148 vs. 60 (Amur), 202 vs. 102 (July), and 267 vs. 92 (graybark). Choice C captures this consistent pattern even though the exact ratio differs by species. Choice B wrongly claims all pairs are opposite-side, and choices A and D focus on comparisons that do not establish the overall trend.

question:
The Age of Innocence is a 1920 novel by Edith Wharton set in 1870s New York City. Early in the novel, Newland Archer arrives late to an opera, and the narrator explains that this is because Newland relishes anticipation: ______

Which quotation from The Age of Innocence best illustrates the claim?
option a: "To come to the Opera in a [carriage for hire] was almost as honourable a way of arriving as in one's own carriage."
option b: "[T]hinking over a pleasure to come often gave [Newland] a subtler satisfaction than its realisation."
option c: "When Newland Archer opened the door at the back of the club box the curtain had just gone up on the garden scene. There was no reason why the young man should not have come earlier, for he had dined at seven, alone with his mother and sister."
option d: "No expense had been spared on the setting, which was acknowledged to be very beautiful even by people who shared [Newland's] acquaintance with the Opera houses of Paris and Vienna."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice B quotes that anticipating a pleasure gave Newland more satisfaction than the pleasure itself, illustrating his enjoyment of anticipation.
longexplanation: The claim explains Newland's lateness by his love of anticipation. Choice B directly states that thinking over a pleasure to come often gave him "a subtler satisfaction than its realisation," capturing that very enjoyment of anticipating. The other quotations concern the respectability of his mode of arrival, the timing of his entrance, or the beauty of the set, none of which illustrate his pleasure in anticipation.

question:
Trade with other societies was essential to the Byzantine Empire, which held sway over the Mediterranean from roughly 330 CE until 1453 CE. Its merchants prospered by selling salt, textiles, and iron—goods that ______ greatly in demand.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The plural subject "goods" (salt, textiles, and iron) requires the plural past-tense verb "were."
longexplanation: The verb refers back to the plural "goods" that were in demand, so a plural verb is needed. "Were" agrees with that plural subject and fits the past-tense context describing the Byzantine Empire. "Has been," "was," and "is" are singular or present tense and do not agree with the plural subject.

question:
On the periodic table, an element's atomic number tells you how many protons a single atom of that element contains. A helium atom, for instance, ______ 2 protons. Professor Raymond Chang lays out this idea more fully in his textbook Chemistry.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A general, timeless fact takes the simple present "has."
longexplanation: The sentence states a permanent scientific fact: a helium atom contains 2 protons. The simple present "has" correctly expresses this ongoing truth. "Has had" and "had" imply completed or past possession, and "is having" wrongly uses the progressive for a fixed, unchanging state.

question:
The observatory sites that make up the Super Dual Auroral Radar Network—SuperDARN, in the shorthand of space physicists like Mark Lester—stretch from Finland to Australia and total nearly five ______ across the globe, the radars track ionospheric irregularities and other geospace phenomena.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A period after "dozen" ends one complete sentence, and "Located" begins a new sentence describing the radars.
longexplanation: The words before the blank form a complete sentence ending in "nearly five dozen," while what follows ("across the globe, the radars track...") is a separate independent clause. Placing a period after "dozen" and starting the next sentence with the modifier "Located" avoids a comma splice and correctly attaches the introductory phrase to "the radars." The other options join two independent clauses with only a comma or leave a dangling fragment.

question:
The giant sequoia (Sequoiadendron giganteum) called D-23, which grows in the United States, ranked among the oldest known trees on Earth at 3,075 years of age. With more than three millennia of climate data recorded in its tree ______ single tree like this, argues dendrochronologist Valerie Trouet, can tell the history of the world.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A comma after "rings" sets off the introductory phrase before the main clause beginning "a single tree."
longexplanation: The opening phrase "With more than three millennia of climate data recorded in its tree rings" modifies the main clause and must be separated from it by a comma. Choice D, "rings, a," supplies that comma and lets "a single tree like this... can tell the history of the world" stand as the main clause. A period or semicolon would wrongly cut the introductory phrase off as a fragment, and "and" would produce a faulty, run-together structure.
